inspiration.observed_pattern: An outer-join regression query uses RIGHT JOIN in a chained join and orders the resulting nullable columns to make preserved right-side rows observable.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an independently authored customer totals report. RIGHT JOIN preserves a customer with no orders, COUNT measures matched order IDs, and COALESCE turns the NULL aggregate for that preserved row into zero. The fixture schema, rows, and reporting purpose are new; PostgreSQL-only view and regression machinery are omitted.

fixture_notes: Customer 1 has two orders, one with a NULL total; customer 2 has one order totaling 7; customer 3 has no orders and must remain in the RIGHT JOIN result with order_count 0 and revenue 0.
determinism_notes: The report is ordered by the unique customer ID. All values are fixed and there are no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections.
setup: CREATE TABLE customers (customer_id INT PRIMARY KEY, customer_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE customer_orders (order_id INT PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INT NOT NULL, order_total INT NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, COALESCE(SUM(o.order_total), 0) AS revenue FROM customer_orders o RIGHT JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name ORDER BY c.customer_id

checks.sql: SELECT customer_id, customer_name FROM customers ORDER BY customer_id
SELECT order_id, customer_id, order_total FROM customer_orders ORDER BY order_id
